mainTopic: Folk remedies in the גמרא: eyes, nosebleeds, blood from the mouth, teeth, gums and ברסם
overview: This amud continues the גמרא's long list of folk remedies. Each one names an illness and then gives the steps to treat it. It starts with cures for eye disease, night blindness and day blindness, several of them rituals with spoken words. Next comes a long chain of backup cures for a nosebleed, each introduced by וְאִי לָא ('and if not'). For blood from the mouth, the גמרא gives a straw test: lung bleeding can be treated, liver bleeding cannot. רב אמי challenges this from a משנה about טריפות, and רב אשי answers that liver blood from the mouth means the liver has dissolved. The גמרא then gives the cure for lung bleeding, a garlic cure for toothache, and a three-stage treatment for gum sores. The amud ends with a remedy for ברסם, a chest illness, whose backup recipe continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A scorpion eye paint for eye disease
steps.stepSummary: For the eye disease called בְּרוּקְתִּי, dry a seven-colored scorpion, grind it with eye paint, and apply exactly three brushfuls to each eye.
steps.simpleTranslation: For eye disease: take a scorpion of seven colors and dry it in the shade. Grind two parts eye paint with one part scorpion. Put three brushfuls in each eye, and no more, or the eye will burst.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a remedy for an eye disease called בְּרוּקְתִּי. It lists the ingredients, the mixture, and the exact dose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The recipe is very precise: a 2-to-1 ratio of eye paint to scorpion, and exactly three brushfuls per eye. The warning at the end shows that the limit on the dose is part of the cure itself. Using too much is dangerous.
steps.confusionAlert: This is a list of medical remedies, not a halachic argument. There is no question and answer here, only instructions, one after another.

phrases.english: For eye disease,
let him bring a scorpion of seven colors,
and dry it in the shade;
and grind two portions of eye paint
and one portion of it;
and let him put three brushfuls in this eye
and three brushfuls in that eye;
more than that he should not put,
for if not, his eye will burst.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the running list of remedies from earlier on the daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For בְּרוּקְתִּי: grind dried seven-colored scorpion with eye paint (1:2) and apply three brushfuls per eye, no more.

steps.title: Night blindness: the dog, the children, and the seven pieces of meat
steps.stepSummary: For night blindness, the patient ties his leg to a dog's leg with a hair rope. Children throw shards and chant behind him. He then eats seven pieces of raw meat collected from seven houses, in the town junk heap.
steps.simpleTranslation: For night blindness: bring a rope of hair and tie one of his legs to one of a dog's legs. Children throw shards behind him and say, 'The dog is old, the rooster is foolish.' Collect seven pieces of raw meat from seven houses, leave them for him in the door socket, and he eats them in the town junk heap.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new remedy, this time for night blindness. This step gives the first part of the ritual. The ending comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the eye paint, this remedy is a ritual with several stages. These include tying the patient to a dog, a chant by children, and gathering meat from seven different houses. The number seven appears again, as it did with the seven-colored scorpion.

keyTerms.meaning: Blindness (here, a kind of poor vision)
A rope made of animal hair

phrases.english: For night blindness,
let him bring a rope of hair,
and tie one leg of his
together with one leg of a dog;
and let children throw shards behind him,
and let them say to him:
"The dog is old, the rooster is foolish";
and let him collect seven pieces of raw meat from seven houses,
and let them be left for him in the socket of the door,
and let him eat them in the junk heap of the town.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next illness on the list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Night blindness is treated by a ritual: tie the patient to a dog, children chant, and the patient eats seven pieces of meat from seven houses in the junk heap.

steps.title: Finishing the night-blindness ritual: untying the rope and the words to say
steps.stepSummary: After eating, the patient unties the hair rope. The words said ask the blindness to leave the person and pass into the dog's eye.
steps.simpleTranslation: Afterward, untie the hair rope and say: 'The blindness of so-and-so son of so-and-so, leave so-and-so son of so-and-so, and let it be blown into the pupil of the dog's eye.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the night-blindness remedy from the previous step. It gives the final action and the words to say.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The dog that was tied to the patient now plays its role. The words send the blindness away from the person and into the dog's eye. The person is named by his mother's name (בַּר פְּלוֹנִיתָא), not his father's.
steps.whatToRemember: The night-blindness cure is one connected ritual: tie the patient to the dog, eat the meat, untie the rope, and send the blindness into the dog's eye.

phrases.english: After this, let him untie the rope of hair,
and let them say as follows:
"The blindness of so-and-so, son of so-and-so (his mother),
let it leave so-and-so, son of so-and-so,
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets; the word in square brackets is the corrected wording. Both basically mean "leave him."

phrases.english: and let them blow into the pupil of the dog's eye."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the night-blindness ritual begun in step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ritual ends by untying the rope and sending the blindness from the patient into the dog's eye.

steps.title: Day blindness: roasted spleens and the 'blind man / seeing man' exchange
steps.stepSummary: For day blindness, the patient roasts seven spleens on a bloodletter's shard. He eats them through an exchange of words with someone outside. Then he breaks the shard so the blindness won't come back.
steps.simpleTranslation: For day blindness: bring seven red parts from inside an animal (spleens) and roast them on a bloodletter's shard. The patient sits inside and another person sits outside. The blind one says to him, 'Give me, so I may eat,' and that other one, the seeing one, answers, 'Take, eat.' After eating, he breaks the shard, or else the blindness returns to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new illness, day blindness, and gives a ritual for curing it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The blind patient inside asks for food, and the seeing person outside hands it to him, so the exchange is between a blind man and a seeing man. The final instruction, breaking the shard, is part of the remedy. Without it, the blindness comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: The pottery shard of a bloodletter

phrases.english: For day blindness,
let him bring seven spleens from inside an animal,
phrases.notes: Literally "seven red ones" from inside an animal, meaning the spleens.

phrases.english: and roast them on the shard of a bloodletter;
and let him sit inside
and another person outside,
and let the blind one say to him: "Give me, so I may eat,"
and let that other one, the seeing one, say to him: "Take, eat";
and after he eats, let him break the shard,
for if not, it will come back upon him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from night blindness to its counterpart, day blindness.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Day blindness is treated by eating seven roasted spleens through a 'blind man / seeing man' exchange, then breaking the shard.

steps.title: Nosebleed: writing a name backward
steps.stepSummary: For a nosebleed, a כֹּהֵן named לֵוִי writes the name לֵוִי backward. If none is available, any person writes 'I am Pappi Sheila bar Summakei' backward.
steps.simpleTranslation: For a nosebleed: bring a man who is a כֹּהֵן named לֵוִי, and he writes 'לֵוִי' backward for the patient. If that is not possible, bring any ordinary person, and he writes 'I am Pappi Sheila bar Summakei' backward.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a remedy for a nosebleed. It offers a main option and a backup option.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The main remedy needs a very specific person: a כֹּהֵן whose name is לֵוִי. Because such a person may be hard to find, the גמרא gives a fallback that any ordinary person can do. In both options the writing must be done backward.

keyTerms.meaning: An ordinary person; anyone at all
And if not (introduces a backup option)

steps.whatToRemember: Each remedy in this list follows one pattern: name the illness (לְ...), then give the steps. Sometimes a warning or a backup option is added at the end.

phrases.english: For blood that comes from the nose,
let him bring a man who is a priest whose name is Levi,
and he should write for him "Levi" backward.
And if not, let him bring an ordinary person,

phrases.aramaic: וְנִיכְתּוֹב לֵיהּ: ״אֲנָא פַּפֵּי שֵׁילָא בַּר סוּמָּקֵי״ – לְמַפְרֵעַ.
phrases.english: and he should write for him: "I am Pappi Sheila bar Summakei", backward.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next illness on the list, a nosebleed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For a nosebleed, a כֹּהֵן named לֵוִי writes 'לֵוִי' backward. Otherwise, anyone writes 'I am Pappi Sheila bar Summakei' backward.

steps.title: A second written formula for a nosebleed
steps.stepSummary: If the earlier written cure does not work, a different phrase is written: 'Taste from a bucket in silver water, taste from a bucket in tainted water.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And if that does not work, let him write this for the patient: 'Taste from a bucket in silver water, taste from a bucket in tainted water.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the next backup cure for a nosebleed. It is another written formula.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This continues the list from Step 5, where the cure was writing a name. The words 'וְאִי לָא' signal a fallback: try this if the earlier option is not available or does not help.

keyTerms.meaning: And if not: if the earlier option is not available or does not work

phrases.english: And if not, let him write for him like this:
phrases.notes: This continues from Step 5: if the earlier writing cure is not possible, write these words instead.

phrases.english: Taste from a bucket in silver water,
taste from a bucket in tainted water.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another fallback to the nosebleed cures from Step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A further nosebleed remedy: write 'taste from a bucket in silver water, taste from a bucket in tainted water.'

steps.title: Wool wicks dipped in vinegar and special ash
steps.stepSummary: Burn five ingredients into ash. Soak two wool wicks in vinegar, roll them in the ash, and put them in the nostrils.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if that does not work, he should take fodder root, rope from an old bed, paper, saffron, and the red part of a palm branch, and burn them all together. Then he spins two strings from wool, soaks them in vinegar, rolls them in the ash, and puts them in his nostrils.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the next fallback for a nosebleed. This one is a physical treatment: wicks placed in the nose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The cures now move from writing to a hands-on treatment. Several ingredients are burned to make ash, and wool wicks carry the vinegar and the ash into the nostrils.

phrases.english: And if not, let him bring the root of fodder,
and rope from an old bed,
and paper, and saffron, and the red part of a palm branch;
and let him burn them together;
and let him bring a fleece of wool
and spin two strings,
and soak them in vinegar,
and roll them in this ash,
and place them in his nostrils.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The next fallback after the written formula in Step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Nosebleed remedy: wool wicks soaked in vinegar and rolled in the ash of five burned ingredients, placed in the nostrils.

steps.title: Wool wicks dipped in clay from an east-to-west stream
steps.stepSummary: The patient stands over a stream flowing east to west and takes clay from under each foot with the opposite hand. He soaks wool wicks in the clay and puts them in his nose.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if that does not work, he should find a stream flowing from east to west and stand with one foot on each side. With his right hand he takes clay from under his left foot, and with his left hand clay from under his right foot. He spins two wool strings, soaks them in the clay, and puts them in his nostrils.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another fallback nosebleed cure. Again wicks go in the nose, but this time they are soaked in clay taken in a very specific way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wicks are the same as in Step 7, but the material changes from vinegar and ash to clay. The details matter: the stream must flow east to west, and each hand takes clay from under the opposite foot.

phrases.english: And if not, let him look for a stream of water
that flows from east toward west;
and let him spread his legs and stand
with one foot on this side
and one foot on that side;
and let him take clay with his right hand
from under his left foot,
and with his left hand from under his right foot;
and let him spin two strings of wool
and soak them in the clay,
and place them in his nostrils.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another fallback. It reuses the wool wicks from Step 7 but soaks them in clay instead.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Nosebleed remedy: wool wicks soaked in clay taken crosswise from both banks of an east-to-west stream, placed in the nostrils.

steps.title: Sitting under a gutter while water is poured
steps.stepSummary: The patient sits under a gutter while water is poured on him. People say: just as this water stopped, may his blood stop.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if that does not work, he should sit under a gutter. People bring water and pour it on him, and they say: 'Just as this water has stopped, may the blood of so-and-so son of so-and-so stop.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the last cure in the nosebleed list. It is an action paired with spoken words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the cure depends on a comparison: the water stops flowing, and the words ask the blood to stop the same way. This matches the earlier night-blindness cure in Step 3, where spoken words asked the illness to leave.
steps.whatToRemember: The nosebleed cures form one long chain. Each 'וְאִי לָא' offers the next option: written formulas, ash wicks, clay wicks, and finally the gutter ritual with words.

phrases.english: And if not, let him sit under the gutter,
and let them bring water and pour it on him,
and let them say: "Just as this water has stopped,
may the blood of so-and-so son of so-and-so stop."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The final fallback in the nosebleed series.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Nosebleed remedy: pour water on the patient under a gutter while saying, 'just as this water stopped, may his blood stop.'

steps.title: Testing blood from the mouth with a wheat straw
steps.stepSummary: Blood from the mouth is tested with a wheat straw. If it sticks, it comes from the lungs and can be treated. If not, it comes from the liver and cannot be treated.
steps.simpleTranslation: For blood that comes from the mouth, we check it with a wheat straw. If it sticks, it is coming from the lungs, and there is a remedy. If not, it is coming from the liver, and there is no remedy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new medical problem: blood coming out of the mouth. It first gives a test to find where the blood is coming from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the earlier steps, this one is a test, not a cure. Whether the blood sticks to the straw tells you its source. The source decides whether a cure is possible: lungs (ריאה) can be treated, liver (כבד) cannot.
steps.confusionAlert: This step starts a new topic. It is not another nosebleed cure, and the 'וְאִי לָא' here does not mean 'if the last cure failed.' It means 'if the blood does not stick.'

phrases.english: For blood that comes from the mouth,
we check it with a straw of wheat,
if it sticks, it is coming from the lungs
and it has a remedy,
and if not, it is coming from the liver
and it has no remedy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the nosebleed list and opens a new topic: blood from the mouth.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Blood from the mouth is tested with a wheat straw. If it sticks, it comes from the lungs and can be treated. If it does not, it comes from the liver and cannot be treated.

steps.title: A משנה seems to say the opposite about lung and liver
steps.stepSummary: רב אמי challenges the claim that lung bleeding can be treated but liver bleeding cannot. He points to a משנה where lung damage is treated as more serious than liver damage.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אמי said to רב אשי: But we learned the opposite in a משנה! An animal is a טריפה if the liver is removed and nothing of it remains, but a lung becomes a טריפה if it is merely punctured or missing a part.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אמי attacks the rule from Step 10, that lung bleeding is curable and liver bleeding is not. He quotes a משנה that seems to point the other way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the laws of טריפות, the liver only makes an animal a טריפה if it is completely gone. The lung makes it a טריפה even from a small hole. That suggests the lung is more fragile than the liver, which is the opposite of Step 10.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַמֵּי לְרַב אָשֵׁי,
phrases.english: Rav Ami said to Rav Ashi:
But didn't we learn the opposite?
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in חולין 42a that lists what makes an animal a טריפה.

phrases.aramaic: נִיטָּל הַכָּבֵד וְלֹא נִשְׁתַּיֵּיר הֵימֶנָּה כְּלוּם,
phrases.english: If the liver was removed and nothing of it remains,
or a lung that was punctured or is missing a part!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the lung/liver rule given in Step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that lung bleeding is curable but liver bleeding is not.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה of טריפות treats the liver as tougher than the lung, since only total loss of the liver is fatal. So liver trouble should be the more survivable one.

steps.title: Blood from the mouth means the liver has dissolved
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that when liver blood reaches the mouth, the liver must already have dissolved. That is why it cannot be treated.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Since the blood is coming out of his mouth, say that the liver has dissolved.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers the challenge. Liver blood coming out of the mouth is a sign that the liver has fallen apart.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה is not contradicted. A liver with some of it remaining can survive. But if liver blood is coming out of the mouth, we assume the whole liver has dissolved. That matches the משנה's case of nothing remaining.

phrases.english: He said to him: Since it comes out from his mouth,
say that it has dissolved.
phrases.notes: He means the liver has fallen apart, so it really is like the משנה's case where nothing of the liver remains.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אמי's challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the case: mouth-bleeding from the liver means total breakdown of the liver.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Liver damage is milder than lung damage, so liver bleeding should be curable.
steps.terutzMaskana: Liver blood coming from the mouth shows the liver has fully dissolved, so it is fatal. This fits the משנה.

steps.title: What is the remedy for lung bleeding?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the earlier line that lung bleeding has a remedy and asks what that remedy is.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: If the blood comes from the lung, it has a remedy. What is its remedy?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the line from Step 10 that lung bleeding can be treated. It is setting up the next step, which gives the actual remedy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 10 promised a cure for lung bleeding but did not say what it is. This question fills in that missing detail.

keyTerms.meaning: the Master said (quoting an earlier statement)

phrases.english: The Master said:
phrases.notes: This quotes the statement from Step 10 about the wheat straw test.

phrases.aramaic: אִי מֵרֵיאָה קָאָתֵי, אִית לֵיהּ תַּקַּנְתָּא.
phrases.english: If it comes from the lung, it has a remedy.
What is its remedy?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר: אִי מֵרֵיאָה קָאָתֵי, אִית לֵיהּ תַּקַּנְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to Step 10's statement after the challenge has been settled.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The specific cure for bleeding that comes from the lungs.

steps.title: The cooked remedy for lung bleeding
steps.stepSummary: The patient cooks and eats a mixture of beets, leek, פרידא grass, lentils, cumin, spices (or ropes) and firstborn intestines. Afterward he drinks strong beer.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let him bring seven fistfuls of sliced beets, seven of sliced leek, five of פרידא, three of lentils, a fistful of cumin and a fistful of spices (or ropes), and an equal amount of firstborn intestines. He cooks and eats it, and afterward drinks good, strong beer.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with a recipe. The patient cooks it, eats it, and then drinks strong beer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The amounts get smaller as the list goes on: seven, seven, five, three, one, one. The intestines are added to match the plant amounts. Drinking strong beer afterward is the last part of the treatment.

phrases.english: Let him bring seven fistfuls of sliced beets,
and seven fistfuls of sliced leek,
and five fistfuls of perida grass,
and three fistfuls of lentils,
and a fistful of cumin, and a fistful of (ropes) [spices];
phrases.notes: Some versions say "ropes," the word in round brackets; the corrected wording, in square brackets, says "spices."

phrases.english: and a corresponding amount of the intestines of a firstborn animal;
and let him cook it and eat it,
and afterward let him drink good, strong beer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A cooked mixture of vegetables, lentils, spices and firstborn intestines, followed by strong beer.
steps.whatToRemember: Lung bleeding can be treated, and the cure is a cooked mixture followed by strong beer. Liver bleeding from the mouth cannot be treated, because it means the liver has dissolved.

steps.title: A garlic cure for toothache
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר רב הונא gives a toothache cure. Ground single-clove garlic is placed on the thumbnail of the side that hurts, inside a ring of dough, so it does not touch the skin.
steps.simpleTranslation: For toothache, רבה בר רב הונא said: Let him take a single-clove garlic and grind it with oil and salt. He puts it on the thumbnail of the side that hurts and surrounds it with a rim of dough. He must be careful it does not touch his flesh, because it is harmful and causes boils.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new illness, toothache, and gives a garlic cure from רבה בר רב הונא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The garlic goes on the thumb of the same side as the pain, not on the tooth itself. The dough ring keeps the strong garlic from touching the skin, since it can cause sores.

keyTerms.meaning: garlic that grew as a single clove

phrases.aramaic: לְכַכָּא – אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא:
phrases.english: For toothache, Rabba bar Rav Huna said:
Let him bring a single-clove garlic
and grind it with oil and salt,
and place it on the thumbnail
of the side that hurts him,
and surround it with a rim of dough.
And he should be careful about his flesh,
because it is harmful and causes boils.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְכַכָּא – אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from bleeding cures to a new ailment, toothache.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For toothache, put ground single-clove garlic with oil and salt on the thumbnail of the painful side, inside a dough ring, keeping it off the skin.

steps.title: Chamomile to calm gum disease
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says Spanish chamomile works like ממרו, and its root works even better. It is held in the mouth to keep gum disease from getting worse.
steps.simpleTranslation: For gums, רבי יוחנן said: Spanish chamomile is like ממרו, and the root of Spanish chamomile is better than ממרו. Let him hold it in his mouth. These are to stabilize the illness.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רבי יוחנן's cure for gum disease. It then explains that this cure is meant to stop the illness from getting worse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן ranks the plants: the chamomile is as good as ממרו, and its root is better still. The closing words 'these are to stabilize' set up a contrast with the next step, which gives a cure for a different goal.

phrases.english: For gums, Rabbi Yochanan said:
Spanish chamomile is like mamru,
and the root of Spanish chamomile is better than mamru,
and let him hold it in his mouth.
These are to stabilize the illness;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to another ailment, gum disease.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Hold Spanish chamomile (best is its root) or ממרו in the mouth to keep gum disease from getting worse.

steps.title: A cure to bring gum sores to a head
steps.stepSummary: To bring gum sores to a head so they open and drain, the patient holds a nut-sized amount of a mixture in his mouth. The mixture is coarse bran, lentils with their dirt, fenugreek and hop flower.
steps.simpleTranslation: To bring the sores to a head: let him bring bran from the top of the sifter, lentils with their dirt, fenugreek, and the flower of hops. Let him hold about a nut's worth in his mouth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second gum cure with a different goal. This one brings the sores to a head, so they are ready to open and let the pus out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 16 was about calming the disease. This step is about pushing it to open and drain. The ingredients are rough ones: coarse bran and lentils that still have dirt on them. A nut-sized portion is held in the mouth.

keyTerms.meaning: to bring to a head (make sores open)

phrases.english: To bring it to a head, let him bring the bran at the top of the sifter,
and lentils with their dirt,
and fenugreek, and the flower of hops,
and let him hold about a nut's worth in his mouth.

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: Part of רבי יוחנן's statement in Step 16
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts with Step 16: there the cure stabilizes, here it brings the sores to a head.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: To make gum sores open, hold a nut-sized amount of coarse bran, dirty lentils, fenugreek and hop flower in the mouth.
steps.whatToRemember: Gum disease has two kinds of cures. One kind keeps it from getting worse (chamomile or ממרו). The other kind makes the sores open and drain (the bran and lentil mixture).

steps.title: How to open the gum sores
steps.stepSummary: To open the gum sores so the pus can drain, a friend blows white cress into the patient's mouth through a wheat straw.
steps.simpleTranslation: To open the sores, his friend should blow white cress into his mouth through a straw of wheat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is still on the gum sores from the last step. Now that the sores have come to a head, it tells us how to open them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The last step got the sores ready to burst. This step is the next stage, actually opening them. The cress is blown in through a thin wheat straw, so it reaches the sore directly.

phrases.english: To open them:
let his friend blow for him
white cress
through a straw of wheat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the next stage of the gum-sore treatment from step 17: opening the sores after they come to a head.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: To open gum sores, a friend blows white cress into the mouth through a wheat straw.

steps.title: How to heal the gum sores
steps.stepSummary: To heal the sores, the patient kneads dirt from the shaded area of a bathroom with honey and eats it.
steps.simpleTranslation: To heal them, he should take dirt from the shade of the bathroom, knead it with honey and eat it, because it helps him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the last stage of the gum-sore treatment: healing the sores after they have been opened.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The order is now complete: first bring the sores to a head, then open them, then heal them. The odd ingredient, dirt from a bathroom's shade, is mixed with honey and eaten.

keyTerms.meaning: to heal (to close up the wound)

steps.whatToRemember: The gum-sore cure has three stages: bring the sores to a head (step 17), open them (step 18), and heal them (step 19).

phrases.english: To heal them:
let him bring dirt from the shade of the bathroom,
and knead it with honey and eat it,
for it is good for him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the gum-sore treatment begun in steps 17 and 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: To heal gum sores, a person eats dirt from a bathroom's shade kneaded with honey.

steps.title: A boiled remedy for a chest illness
steps.stepSummary: For ברסם, a person boils נשדור, sweet galbanum, white honey and clear wine together. Once the נשדור is cooked, the whole mixture is ready.
steps.simpleTranslation: For ברסם, take a pistachio-sized amount of נשדור, a nut-sized amount of sweet galbanum, a full spoon of white honey, and a full מחוזא-style cup of clear wine. Boil them all together. When the נשדור is cooked, everything is cooked.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new illness, ברסם, and gives a recipe for it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a new topic, not part of the gum-sore cure. The recipe lists exact amounts of four ingredients. It also gives an easy sign of when it is done: once the נשדור is cooked, the whole mixture is ready.

keyTerms.meaning: an illness of the chest or breathing passages
נשדור, an ingredient in the remedy
a cup of the kind used in מחוזא

phrases.english: For ברסם:
phrases.notes: This is an illness of the chest or breathing passages.

phrases.english: let him bring a pistachio-sized amount of נשדור,
and a nut-sized amount of sweet galbanum,
and a full spoon of white honey,
and a full מחוזא-style cup
of clear wine;
and let him boil them all together;
and when the נשדור is cooked,
the whole mixture is cooked.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the gum sores and starts a remedy for a new illness, ברסם.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For ברסם, boil נשדור, sweet galbanum, white honey and clear wine together until the נשדור is cooked.

steps.title: A backup remedy with white goat's milk
steps.stepSummary: If the first ברסם remedy is not possible, the person should instead use a רביעית of milk from a white goat. The recipe continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if he cannot do that, he should bring a רביעית of milk from a white goat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a second, backup remedy for ברסם, for someone who cannot make the first one. The details continue on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words "and if not" tell us this is a replacement for the boiled wine mixture, not an extra step added to it. The milk must come from a white goat. The rest of the instructions continue on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: and if not (if he cannot do the first remedy)
a quarter-log, a small measure of liquid

phrases.english: And if not:
let him bring a quarter-log of milk
from a white goat
phrases.notes: The sentence keeps going on the next amud, where the rest of the recipe is given.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a replacement remedy for ברסם, in case the step 20 mixture cannot be made.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the first remedy cannot be made, use a quarter-log of white goat's milk. The instructions continue.
